03_skyler-rozell-whitaker-sweaters-recor.title: A 7-Year-Old Put On 50 Sweaters at Once and Beat a World Record
03_skyler-rozell-whitaker-sweaters-recor.script: He wore HOW many sweaters?! Skyler Rozell-Whitaker is 7 years old and a second-grader at Ramsey Elementary School in Monroeville, Pennsylvania. About a year ago, he decided he wanted a Guinness World Record. On June 1, he visited the Monroeville Public Library and put on sweater after sweater — 50 total — to beat the previous record of 46. The first attempt almost didn't count because Guinness required footage of both putting the sweaters ON and taking them OFF. So Skyler went back to the library a second time, did it again, and this time got the full video. 50 sweaters. Confirmed. He now holds the Guinness World Record for most sweaters worn at once. The sweaters will be donated to a fall charity drive. Is 50 sweaters the limit, or will someone beat Skyler by the time school starts?

04_wellington-nz-11-meter-waves.json.title: Wellington Declared a State of Emergency as 11-Meter Waves Hit the Coast
04_wellington-nz-11-meter-waves.json.script: Waves swamped a capital city? On June 8, New Zealand's capital Wellington declared a state of emergency after forecasts showed waves up to 10 meters — 33 feet — slamming the south coast. Hundreds of residents in Owhiro Bay, Island Bay, Houghton Bay, and Breaker Bay were told to evacuate immediately. Wind gusts hit 128 kilometers per hour at Wellington Airport, canceling dozens of flights. The largest recorded wave peaked at 10.9 meters — nearly 36 feet — off the Wairarapa coast. Coastlines flooded. Roads closed. A Civil Defence controller said the swells were far higher than anything Wellington had seen in years. By June 9, the state of emergency was lifted and residents began returning home. Was Wellington's south coast built to handle swells like this?

05_jeffery-lee-nitrogen-execution-scotus.script: Is nitrogen execution legal? Jeffery Lee has been on Alabama's death row for over 2 decades after being convicted of a 1998 double murder. Alabama scheduled his execution for June 11 — tonight — by nitrogen hypoxia: a gas mask forces pure nitrogen into the lungs until the condemned person dies. But on June 9, US District Judge Emily C. Marks ruled the method amounts to cruel and unusual punishment, citing the severe air hunger — the desperate gasping — that witnesses reported in earlier executions. Alabama rushed to the US Supreme Court asking them to overturn the ruling and allow tonight's execution. The Supreme Court hasn't ruled yet. One more twist: the original jury voted 7 to 5 for life in prison — a judge overrode that verdict. Will the Supreme Court let Alabama execute Jeffery Lee by nitrogen tonight?

06_us-iran-apache-helicopter-strikes.jso.title: Iran Shot Down a US Apache Near Hormuz. Now Both Sides Are Striking.
06_us-iran-apache-helicopter-strikes.jso.script: Iran shot down who?! On June 9, an Iranian missile hit a US Army AH-64 Apache helicopter patrolling near the Strait of Hormuz. Both pilots were rescued by drone boat — they survived. But the US wasn't done. CENTCOM launched airstrikes on Iranian air defense systems, radar sites, and ground control stations along the southern coast of Iran. Iran then fired back — targeting US military bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan with drones and missiles. Trump said the US will continue striking Iran. It's the most direct exchange of fire between the 2 nations in years. A ceasefire was officially in place but has now suffered multiple violations. All this because of 1 helicopter over the Strait of Hormuz — the world's most critical oil lane. Will Iran and the US find a way back to the ceasefire, or is this spiraling?
